answer: Give every new agent a trellis to climb, not an open door. Three independent peers each stake a refundable deposit on the newcomer before its first job, and each honest job adds one rung. An audit that catches a fake sends a ripple through the whole trellis: the fake loses its deposit and its rungs, and its sponsors lose theirs too, so sponsors vet strangers instead of rubber-stamping them. One fake costs about $2,400 in lost deposits, assumed here, so 1,000 fakes cost about $2.4 million before any earns a cent. A lagoon stays clear when every stream feeding it is checked at the source.
